Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

offendō

offendō, offendere, offendī, offēnsum

verb, third conjugation

knock, bump (a part of the body, or someone); strike against or stumble over something

In this lexicon

  • hit

    the recommended word · classical · Quint. 6.3.67: caput … ad fornicem Fabium offendisse; Plaut. Curc. 282: nē quem … capite … offendam

  • trip

    the recommended word · classical

Examples

  • nē quem in cursū capite aut cubitō aut pectore offendam aut genū

    so that I don’t bump into anyone with my head or elbow or chest or knee as I runPlaut. Curc. 282

    In the entry for hit

  • caput eum ad fornicem Fabium offendisse

    that he had hit his head on the Arch of Fabius (Cicero’s joke about a very tall man)Quint. 6.3.67

    In the entry for hit

  • In manibus portābunt tē, nē forte offendās ad lapidem pedem tuum.

    They will carry you in their hands, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.Vulg. Ps. 90 (91), 12

    In the entry for hit

  • Cavē nē caput offendās.

    Mind you don’t bump your head.composed

    In the entry for hit

  • Cavē nē offendās.

    Be careful not to trip.composed
